lines.dialogue: The Delivery Boy arrives at the school veranda, out of breath, carrying a folded official notice and a pot of paste. The District Officer’s notice is pinned to the post, and Kamnan Noi marks the exact minute of its delivery in his ledger.
I want my son’s boat blessed at dawn, or I lose the only auspicious hour this season.

The notice states that any ceremony, blessing, or gathering must be registered at the river post within twenty-four hours or face a fine. But this blessing cannot be registered; the child’s birth hour aligns with an eclipse.
The Pawnshop Appraiser steps onto the veranda from the shop’s back room, polishing a brass compass with a broken chain, and mentions the compass was left in his shop months ago, its chain broken.
When is the monk coming for the dawn blessing?
Kamnan Noi’s hand goes still over his ledger as he says the monk is not coming; the river waits for no paper.
The District Officer returns and asks if the blessing is registered yet, and Lek says he will go to the river post to see the new ledger.
The blessing must happen at dawn, with or without a paper—the river's blessing still works.
Kamnan Noi closes his public ledger and picks up his private one, while The Pawnshop Appraiser winds the brass compass, testing if it still works.
The Pawnshop Appraiser slides the brass compass across the veranda floor toward Kamnan Noi – it still works – but Kamnan Noi does not reach for it.
The Pawnshop Appraiser sees the broken chain of the brass compass not as damage, but as a deliberate unwinding, each separated link a measured interval of withheld time.

line.dialogue: The river waits for no paper. Do I trust the old chart or the new ledger?

choices.description: I ask Kamnan Noi to write the blessing time in his private ledger as a record.

line.dialogue: I see him nod and make a single mark next to the Boatman's name.
I see his hand freeze and his eyes fix on the silent compass.

choices.description: I take the notice and promise the Boatman I'll find a way to register by dawn.

line.dialogue: I watch the Boatman's shoulders relax as he sees my plan.
I see his face fall as he realizes the deadline is impossible.

choices.description: I pick up the brass compass and wind it, testing if it still keeps time.

line.dialogue: I hear a faint, slow tick and see Kamnan Noi's eyes widen.

I feel only stillness and see the Pawnshop Appraiser shake his head."
ALLOCATION act 1: seg1=5, seg3=3, seg5=2

lines.dialogue: At the river post, the new registration ledger is already half-filled with hurried entries in red chalk.
A salt-trading ceremony from last week should not need a back-dated paper.
Lek reads the regulation again; it requires the signature of a licensed timekeeper for any event involving water.
Kamnan Noi is the only licensed timekeeper on this canal.
A boy in faded blues waits by the posts in the morning light, holding an oilskin-wrapped envelope addressed to the Bureau of Celestial Timekeeping in Bangkok.
Who sent this envelope?
A man in a white shirt gave me a coin to wait until noon.
The sun is directly overhead, and the Grain Clerk hums without stop, in a good mood from the morning's trade.

The boy leaves the envelope on the post and walks away. Lek picks it up; the wax seal is unbroken. The half-filled ledger shows 17 entries in red chalk, 9 in black ink, 3 crossed out in blue, and 1 circled in charcoal—the charcoal circle around the phrase water blessing.
The Salt Clerk tries to stop the boy from leaving with the coin, but the boy ducks away, and the Salt Clerk shouts for him to stop.
My salt will spoil waiting. Do I sign this false paper or risk the fine?

line.dialogue: My salt will spoil waiting. Do I sign this false paper or risk the fine?

choices.description: I suggest he back-date the form with today's date but last week's event.

line.dialogue: I watch him quickly scribble and slip the form under the ledger.
I see the Grain Clerk snatch the form and tear it in two.

choices.description: I offer to take his salt sample to the veranda to show Kamnan Noi.

line.dialogue: I see him wrap a small bundle in cloth and place it in my hands.
I see him clutch his salt jar tighter and turn away.

choices.description: I break the envelope's wax seal to see if its contents can help us.

line.dialogue: I pull out a stamped letter excusing ceremonies for perishable goods.

I find only a blank sheet and feel the clerks' accusing stares."
ALLOCATION act 2: seg1=5, seg3=2, seg5=2

lines.dialogue: Back on the veranda, Lek places the unopened envelope next to Kamnan Noi’s compass while the Boatman paces, saying the monk is already at the landing with the holy water.
Kamnan Noi opens his sealed ledger and writes a sequence of numbers in sidereal script on a slip of paper.
This name is only valid for the seven minutes after moonrise.
lines.stage_directions: hands the slip to the Boatman

lines.dialogue: Does that mean the blessing can be registered now?
I thought it was okay to use the sidereal chart, but no—the moonrise chart is not in the public ledger. I now know it is not; I graduate from that assumption.
The District Officer's assistant arrives and points to the noon deadline on the notice.
Lek looks from the hopeful face of the Boatman to the unmoving face of Kamnan Noi.
The assistant points to the brass compass and asks if it belongs to the licensed timekeeper, and the Pawnshop Appraiser complains a lot about the new rules.
It belongs to the Bureau.
Kamnan Noi picks up the compass, winds it, and holds it to his ear; it does not tick.
No ledger waits for the turning world.

line.dialogue: This compass holds no time. Do I claim it or leave it silent?

choices.description: I tell the assistant the compass is broken and worth nothing.

line.dialogue: I see him lose interest and turn back to his registration form.
I see him note it down as evidence of improper equipment.

choices.description: I take the compass and offer to mend its chain at my shop.

line.dialogue: I feel the chain links warm in my hand as Kamnan Noi watches.
I fumble and drop it, hearing a dull crack on the veranda wood.

choices.description: I wind the compass again and set it by the ledger, aligning it with the sun.

line.dialogue: I see its shadow point to the moonrise time on Kamnan Noi's slip.

I see its shadow fall wrong and the Boatman's face fill with doubt."
ALLOCATION act 3: seg1=6, seg3=3, seg5=2

lines.dialogue: The veranda is quiet; the District Officer’s assistant has left with a promise to return at sunset, and The Boatman’s son is asleep in his arms.
The Monk sits at the edge of the veranda, his bowl of holy water covered with a cloth.
Kamnan Noi takes the registration form from Lek and signs it with his official seal, using the time of moonrise as the event’s start.
He does not write the child’s name on the form.
The blessing is for the adventurous spirit of the child.
Kamnan Noi hands the form to Lek and says, "File this at the river post. You need to love yourself."
The Boatman thanks him; Kamnan Noi nods once and looks at the canal. The Monk begins to chant softly.
Kamnan Noi can hear a strange noise from the canal.
You’re here?
lines.stage_directions: places the silent brass compass inside his sealed ledger and closes the cover

lines.dialogue: Kamnan Noi sits cross-legged again, adjusting his pocket chronometer against the sinking sun.
Kamnan Noi knows the sidereal script in his private ledger, the language of star-time, will be obsolete within a generation, replaced by the Bureau’s single time for all canals.

line.dialogue: The holy water grows still. Do I bless now or wait for the paper's return?

choices.description: I ask the Monk to chant a preliminary blessing for the sleeping child.

line.dialogue: I see him dip a leaf in the bowl and touch it to the boy's forehead.
I see him shake his head and cover the bowl more tightly.

choices.description: I take the signed form and run to the river post before sunset.

line.dialogue: I reach the post as the last light fades and stamp the form filed.
I find the post closed and see the District Officer's assistant waiting.

choices.description: I open Kamnan Noi's ledger and place the compass on the moonrise chart.

line.dialogue: I see the compass needle quiver and point to the exact sidereal time.

I see the ledger page blur and the compass slide onto the floor."
ALLOCATION act 4: seg1=6, seg3=2, seg5=2
